question: Why is the power of compound interest easy to underestimate?
options: It is illegal in some places

group.title: Reading comprehension
group.setup: Compound interest is often called the most powerful force in personal finance, yet its power is easy to underestimate because it works slowly at first. In the early years, a savings account seems to grow only by the money put into it; the interest feels trivial. Only after a decade or more does the interest earned each year begin to rival the deposits themselves. This is why those who start saving early, even in small amounts, often end up ahead of those who save larger sums later. The same arithmetic works against borrowers: an unpaid credit card balance grows in exactly the way a patient saver's account does.
